parties: Jio Platforms Limited (subsidiary of Reliance Industries Limited)
headline: Jio Platforms files DRHP for India's largest IPO - fresh issue of 270 million equity shares (₹10 face value) targeting ~$3.8 billion raise; legal advisors SAM, CAM, K&Co, Latham & Watkins, White & Case.
sum: Jio Platforms Limited filed its DRHP with SEBI on 19 June 2026 for a 100% fresh equity issue of up to 270 million shares (face value ₹10 each), targeting approximately $3.8 billion in capital raise, positioned as India's largest-ever IPO. The transaction is stewarded by a consortium of India's premier corporate counsel-Shardul Amarchand Mangaldas (lead, Indian law), Cyril Amarchand Mangaldas, and Khaitan & Co-alongside international counsel Latham & Watkins and White & Case (Rule 144A/Regulation S).
implication: The pure-fresh-issue structure (zero OFS) is atypical for an IPO of this scale and signals Reliance's confidence in future capital requirements while preserving all existing investor stakes-a precedent in mega-cap IPO structuring that may reshape multi-asset conglomerate listing strategy.
detail: Jio Platforms, the digital and telecom arm of Reliance Industries, filed its Draft Red Herring Prospectus (DRHP) with SEBI on 19 June 2026-the same day Mukesh Ambani announced it at RIL's 49th AGM. The IPO comprises a 100% book-built fresh issue of up to 27 crore (270 million) equity shares, each with a face value of ₹10; no Offer for Sale component, meaning all net proceeds flow to the company for debt reduction at subsidiary Reliance Jio Infocomm. The offering targets a raise of approximately $3.8 billion (₹360 billion), which if achieved would make it India's largest maiden public issue, surpassing Hyundai Motor India's 2024 record of $3.3 billion. Post-IPO valuation is estimated at $130–180 billion. The company's net debt stood at ₹27,579 crore as of March 2026. Rajagopal Venkatakrishnan, a 30+ year veteran with Reliance tenure since 2015, was appointed General Counsel of Jio Platforms on 1 June 2026. Notably, Haigreve Khaitan (K&Co Managing Partner) and Zia Jaydev Mody (AZB & Partners Co-founder) serve as independent directors on Jio's board, creating a direct overlap between legal counsel and board governance.

structure.novel: 100% fresh equity issuance (zero OFS) in a marquee-scale IPO; no existing shareholder exits; all capital raised flows to subsidiary debt reduction (Reliance Jio Infocomm foreign currency borrowings). This pure growth-capital model is rare in mega-cap public markets and signals exceptional post-listing capex/deleveraging mandate.
